clips.text_zh: 又見到呢啲post。Biz佬話兩個BTC規則撞咗:1D 200SMA突破同4年cycle。底部58k兩個月前已經見?咁bear market得6個月?我學費又交多一次。Wtf。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: An unbreakable rule of crypto has just broken. Rule 1: breaking out from the 1D 200sma after a bear market starts the next bull run. Rule 2: the 4 year cycle. If this is the start of the next bullrun, the bottom was 58k two months ago.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread arguing two BTC cycle rules can't both be true.
clips.text_en_b2: Crypto's so-called unbreakable rules are clashing head-on right now. Rule one says that breaking out above the 1D 200SMA after a bear market kicks off the next bull run. Rule two insists on the four-year cycle. If we take rule one seriously, the bottom at 58k was already in two months ago, which means the bear market barely lasted six months instead of the expected twelve. Because these two rules cannot coexist at this stage of the cycle, one of them is already failing.
clips.text_en_c1: One of crypto's so-called unbreakable rules has apparently just been violated, which is precisely the kind of thing that forces traders to confront their priors. The first principle states that decisively reclaiming the daily 200 SMA ought to mark the inception of a fresh bull cycle. The second insists upon a roughly four-year cadence. If we take the breakout as our cue, then the cyclical bottom was already registered at fifty-eight thousand dollars a mere two months ago, implying that the bear phase lasted only six months rather than the expected twelve.
clips.text_en_c2: Two axioms that the crypto faithful have long treated as gospel appear, on current evidence, to be on a collision course. The first dictates that a decisive break above the daily 200-day simple moving average, following a prolonged downturn, inaugurates the subsequent bull cycle. The second posits the orthodox four-year cadence that has governed Bitcoin's macro rhythm since inception. If, as the price action now suggests, the cyclical low was registered around the fifty-eight thousand dollar threshold a mere two months past, then the preceding bear regime would have lasted barely six months — a duration wholly at odds with the roughly twelve-month baseline the community has internalised. Since both propositions cannot hold simultaneously at this juncture, one must be quietly breaking down. And, judging by the trades, the tuition is being paid.again.

clips.text_zh: 睇到笑出聲。BTC橫盤幾星期你睇都唔睇,升咗15%個個仆晒過去。咪就係我。每次都係咁。命理都寫我遲到。Lol。👍
clips.text_en_b1: Why buy BTC after the pump? You watch BTC do nothing for weeks, ignore it completely. Then it pumps 15% and suddenly everyone wants in. Why does everyone want to buy after the move already happened? This came up on /biz/ today and honestly it describes most retail traders perfectly.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread roasting retail buyers who chase pumps.
clips.text_en_b2: Why does everyone pile into BTC only after it has already moved? You spend weeks watching it go nowhere and refuse to look at it twice, but the moment it pumps 15% the whole crowd scrambles to get in. The pattern is so predictable that it has become a running joke on /biz/. Although retail traders keep swearing they will buy the dip next time, they almost never do. It captures retail behaviour perfectly.
clips.text_en_c1: The perennial retail trading paradox surfaced again on /biz/, and the responses were almost comically on the nose. For several weeks, bitcoin traded sideways within a tight range, during which period the broader crowd ignored it entirely, treating the asset as though it were scenery. The moment price ripped fifteen percent in a single move, however, FOMO descended and everybody wanted a seat at the table. The thread essentially describes a behavioural pattern whereby investors consistently arrive after the opportunity has materially presented itself, and it captures the retail archetype with uncomfortable precision. https://boards.4chan.org/biz/thread/62625769
clips.text_en_c2: It is, frankly, a phenomenon so recurrent that it has acquired the status of market folklore. Bitcoin idles sideways for weeks on end, attracting nothing but indifference from the retail cohort, who cannot be bothered to glance at a chart that refuses to move. Then, without ceremony, price erupts by some fifteen percent in short order, and suddenly the very same population materialises en masse, fumbling for the buy button as though the move itself constituted a personal invitation. A thread on the business board surfaced this exact behavioural signature today, and to its credit the post scarcely needs embellishment, since it captures with uncomfortable precision the reflexivity, the herd-mentality impatience, and the latent FOMO that define the average retail participant. Whichever way one frames it, the punchline writes itself.

clips.text_zh: 嘩。Anthropic同IPO投資者講TAM超過30兆美金,即美計全個美國GDP。舊年虧損420億,2028預測收入190-200兆,尋求2兆估值。我份工好似廢柴。靠AI續命。🧐
clips.text_en_b1: Anthropic is expected to tell IPO investors that its total addressable market exceeds $30 trillion. That is roughly the entire GDP of the United States. TAM is the revenue a company could theoretically earn if it captured 100% of its market. The company lost $42 billion last year, projects $190 to $200 billion in revenue by 2028, and is seeking a $2 trillion valuation.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread on Anthropic's $30 trillion TAM claim for AI work.
clips.text_en_b2: Anthropic is reportedly preparing to tell IPO investors that its total addressable market tops $30 trillion, which is roughly the entire GDP of the United States. TAM, for the uninitiated, is the theoretical revenue a company could grab if it cornered 100% of its market. Although the firm posted a $42 billion loss last year, it is projecting $190 to $200 billion in revenue by 2028 while seeking a $2 trillion valuation. The numbers are frankly absurd.
clips.text_en_c1: Anthropic is reportedly preparing to brief prospective IPO investors on a total addressable market figure that exceeds thirty trillion dollars, a sum that effectively equals the entire GDP of the United States. For those unfamiliar with the acronym, TAM refers to the theoretical maximum revenue a company could capture were it to monopolise every conceivable customer in its category. Against that backdrop, the company's forty-two-billion-dollar loss last year looks less catastrophic than one might assume, particularly given its projected hundred-and-ninety to two-hundred-billion-dollar revenue target by 2028 and the eye-watering two-trillion-dollar valuation it is currently said to be pursuing. https://boards.4chan.org/g/thread/109649964
clips.text_en_c2: Anthropic is reportedly preparing to present prospective IPO investors with a total addressable market estimate that eclipses thirty trillion dollars — a figure that, taken at face value, would approximate the entirety of United States gross domestic product, give or take a few hundred basis points. TAM, for the uninitiated, denotes the theoretical revenue ceiling a firm could capture were it to monopolise its designated market without competition, so the implicit ambition here borders on the cosmological. Against this rather stratospheric backdrop, the company's financials reveal losses of forty-two billion dollars over the trailing year, with management projecting revenues somewhere between one hundred ninety and two hundred billion by 2028. The valuation being courted reportedly stands at two trillion dollars.

clips.text_en_b2: The US Justice Department has seized China-sponsored hacking platforms in a sweeping crackdown. Officials are describing the operation as the largest attack on American infrastructure since Pearl Harbor and the Gulf of Tonkin combined, according to a Reuters report dated August 26, 2026. While the full extent of the damage is still being assessed, the scale is being labelled unprecedented. For once, this is the sort of geopolitical news that genuinely matters.
clips.text_en_c1: According to a Reuters report dated the twenty-sixth of August, 2026, the US Justice Department has successfully dismantled hacking infrastructure that officials have attributed to state-sponsored Chinese actors. Senior figures within the department have gone so far as to characterise the cumulative scale of the intrusion as the most consequential assault on American interests since Pearl Harbor and the Gulf of Tonkin combined, which is not the sort of rhetorical flourish that bureaucrats deploy lightly. If that framing is even remotely accurate, the implications for ongoing diplomatic and cyber-defence posture are considerable, and the situation bears close attention. https://boards.4chan.org/pol/thread/541484633
clips.text_en_c2: Reuters, in a dispatch dated the twenty-sixth of August 2026, reports that the United States Department of Justice has successfully dismantled a constellation of hacking platforms operating under the sponsorship of the Chinese state. Senior officials, never ones to understate matters of national gravity, have characterised the cumulative breach as the most egregious incursion suffered by the republic since Pearl Harbor and the Gulf of Tonkin incident combined — a comparison that, rhetorical flourishes aside, situates the episode firmly within the canon of assaults that genuinely warranted the epithet 'unprecedented'. The Hong Kong corollary, naturally, follows the same template of digital attrition. For once, the news cycle has produced something that merits the attention it is receiving, and the administration appears, for the moment, neither inclined nor able to downplay the severity of the intrusion.

Furthermore, what are the chances that 1 hour before the Netflix presentation CyberLeek drops a HUGE bomb to step all over Rockstars release? Honestly at this point just close the stream.

clips.text_en_b2: Every piece of GTA VI gameplay worth seeing has already been dumped by CyberLeek, so Rockstar's Netflix presentation tomorrow is essentially a tough sell. What on earth can they possibly show that would top what has already leaked online? Chances are CyberLeek drops another massive bombshell right before the stream goes live, completely stealing the spotlight. clips.text_en_c1: The irony of tomorrow's much-hyped Netflix presentation for Grand Theft Auto VI is that virtually every gameplay sequence anybody wanted to see has already surfaced online, courtesy of leaker CyberLeek. The legitimate reveal therefore finds itself in the unenviable position of having to outdo material that audiences have already consumed, dissected, and formed opinions upon. What are the odds, furthermore, that CyberLeek times one final enormous drop for the hour immediately preceding the broadcast, deliberately sabotaging the marketing apparatus that Rockstar has so carefully constructed? At this juncture, one might reasonably question whether the stream should simply be cancelled. https://boards.4chan.org/v/thread/746238319
clips.text_en_c2: Every morsel of footage that anyone might have wished to witness at tomorrow's livestreamed unveiling has, courtesy of the leakers' guild, already been disseminated across the customary back channels of the internet. The question that therefore presents itself is an almost philosophical one — what on earth does Rockstar propose to showcase at a Netflix-adjacent broadcast that could conceivably eclipse material which has been public knowledge for the better part of a week? More pressingly still, what are the realistic odds that, with timing one can only describe as cosmically spiteful, CyberLeek elects to drop an eleventh-hour payload of devastating magnitude precisely one hour before Rockstar takes the stage — an act so theatrical it would render the entire corporate event superfluous? Honestly, at this juncture, the prudent course of action would be to cancel…

clips.text_zh: 都係講中我。$1,500 budget搞home gym,cardio自己搞掂晒。要maximize gains應該買咩?肥仔信今日又叫我gym,我話屋企練算。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: I got $1,500 to spend on home gym equipment. Cardio is taken care of. What would /fit/ buy to maximize gains? The thread is full of people telling him to skip machines and buy a rack, a barbell, plates and a bench. Someone argued $1.5k is plenty if you buy used plates and skip the cable attachments for now.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread asking what to buy with a $1,500 home gym budget.
clips.text_en_b2: I have got $1,500 to kit out a home gym, and cardio is already sorted. What should /fit/ pick up to maximise gains without wasting a cent? The consensus in the thread is to skip machines entirely and go straight for a solid rack, a decent barbell, a bench and a decent set of plates. One user pointed out that $1.5k is plenty if you buy used plates and hold off on cable attachments for now.
clips.text_en_c1: A /fit/ user presented the board with a fifteen-hundred-dollar budget for assembling a home gym, having already arranged for cardiovascular work to be handled separately, and solicited advice on which purchases would most effectively maximise hypertrophy and strength gains. The thread's consensus, delivered with characteristic bluntness, was that machines ought to be disregarded entirely in favour of a power rack, an Olympic barbell, a quality bench, and a used set of plates. Several respondents argued that this allocation is more than sufficient provided one exercises patience, sources plates second-hand, and postpones cable attachments for a later purchasing cycle. https://boards.4chan.org/fit/thread/77474503
clips.text_en_c2: Operating with a modest budget of fifteen hundred dollars and an evident desire to keep cardiovascular conditioning off the equipment list, the original poster solicited counsel on how to maximise hypertrophy per square foot of floor space. The thread, as one might anticipate, descended swiftly into something resembling a sectarian debate, with one camp insisting — not without justification — that any rational allocation would prioritise the foundational quartet of a sturdy rack, an Olympic barbell, a graded set of plates, and a flat bench, while eschewing altogether the chrome-plated distractions of cable crossovers and Smith machines.

clips.text_zh: The Big O。如果Batman冇咁廢會係點,呢套就係答案。我嗰陣Gundam 00迷,都會記得呢部。回味。👍
clips.text_en_b1: The Big O. Anyone remember this anime? It is pretty cool. If you ever wondered what it would be like if Batman did not suck, then this is what you should watch. The series ran 26 episodes and the giant robot style mixes well with the noir detective setting. It still holds up honestly.
clips.source_hint: /a/ thread recommending the retro mecha-noir anime The Big O.
clips.text_en_b2: The Big O is one of those anime that really sticks with you. Although it ran for only 26 episodes, the series blends noir detective storytelling with giant robot action in a way that feels surprisingly fresh even today. Someone summed it up perfectly on the thread, saying it is basically what Batman would be like if Batman actually had a backbone. If you have not given it a shot, it still holds up.
clips.text_en_c1: For those who harbour lingering curiosity regarding The Big O, the Sunrise mecha-noir series remains a surprisingly rewarding watch decades on. The premise essentially asks what Batman might have been had he been written as a compelling protagonist rather than a brooding cipher, and the answer proves far more stylish than one might anticipate. Across its twenty-six episodes, the programme fuses the dramatic weight of retro-futuristic giant-robot combat with the moody atmospherics of classic detective fiction, and the genres coexist in a manner that ought by rights to feel incongruous yet somehow does not. https://boards.4chan.org/a/thread/290215188
clips.text_en_c2: The Big O occupies a peculiar and rather hallowed position within the pantheon of mecha-noir hybrids, a genre so underpopulated that virtually any addition to its canon is cause for quiet celebration among devotees. The premise, reduced to its essentials, asks a deceptively simple counterfactual — what might Gotham have resembled had its masked protector been marginally less brooding and substantially more competent at the actual business of crime-fighting? — and proceeds to answer it over the course of twenty-six episodes whose interplay between noir-inflected detective storytelling and lumbering giant-robot theatrics remains, to this day, remarkably deft. For those who came of age marinating in Gundam 00 and its ilk, the series retains an enduring nostalgic pull, and even viewed with contemporary eyes it withstands scrutiny with admirable composure.
